answer: Price identity in dedicated disk that cannot be shared, not in time or RAM. Each mint must store a large, uniquely seeded dataset — a shale-dense vault of pseudo-random bytes gigabytes wide — and answer random retrieval probes proving it still holds specific offsets. Storing another persona's data means buying another disk; one host cannot let a garden of fakes share a single volume, since each faces independent offset challenges that overlap cannot satisfy. A thousand identities need a thousand full datasets at once, capping fleet size at real cost per head.
